description: The BGS Infiltration SuDS Map gives a preliminary indication of whether the ground can take infiltration sustainable drainage systems such as soakaways, infiltration basins and trenches and permeable pavements. It is structured around four factors: severe constraints to consider first, drainage potential from permeability and depth to groundwater, the risk of ground instability when water infiltrates (soluble rocks, collapsible or compressible ground, running sand, shallow mining, landslides, shrink-swell clays) and the protection of groundwater quality. The British Geological Survey builds it from 15 national subsurface datasets for planners, designers and local authorities that approve SuDS. Coverage is Great Britain at 1:50 000 scale. Format and access: GIS polygon data in ESRI or MapInfo formats, licensed from BGS. Licence and cost: a premium commercial product priced per unit area, with further fees by number of users. Caveats: it is a screening tool, not a substitute for site investigation, and some inputs are modelled, not observed. It supports green infrastructure siting and climate adaptation of urban drainage. Related catalogue records are the CIRIA SuDS Manual and the susdrain SuDS case studies, which describe the designs the map screens.
